intro: To create the ideal fishing setup, begin by selecting the appropriate rods. These rods are part of the diverse gear and tackle options available at the Shop in each reserve. Each rod boasts unique stats that must be considered when pairing it with reels, lines, baits, and other components. This page provides a complete list of all the rods in the game, along with their key statistics.
Give it a go. Let’s see what amazing fishing setup you come up with. 🎣

items.name: Ace High
items.about: This rod requires the Mountain Range Pack DLC.

items.name: Advocate
items.about: The Advocate is tailor made for empathic anglers who prefer to feel while they fish, connecting with the catch on a fundamental level. It’s for the sensitive angler who explores the world within themselves before they take a step outside.

items.name: Ankaret
items.about: The Ankaret feels like a weighty, well constructed rod that would be the most ostentatious and eye-catching piece on any other brand’s menu, but for Fiskesprö it’s just another entry. If you’d like to dip your toe into a pond of unpleasant and disagreeable braggadocio, this will help you make the plunge.

items.name: Architect
items.about: The Architect is a rod balanced for the careful and intuitive thinker that plans out their trajectory extensively before considering a catch. It is a perfect compliment to a measured mind, and for that personality type offers a formidable fishing experience like no other.

items.name: B44 Trigger
items.about: The B44 Trigger has been cobbled and stiched expertly out of shotgun parts, offering a frankly obscene amount of power in a reasonably priced package. The Trigger is something explosive that will certainly disturb the peace, but may not quite offer the reach of its peers.

items.name: Brass Monkey
items.about: The Brass Monkey is a mainstay of the historical Wright lineup, proving to be a particularly popular form factor throughout the brand’s lengthy reign as the strong arm and long reach of Britain’s working class. This particular rod was much loved by the miners of Hartlepool, who found the extra casting exertion required kept them warm in even the harshest northern winters; the rod slotting seamlessly into their traditional winter wear, a pair of shorts and a blue-and-white striped polyester vest.

items.name: Buckwheat
items.about: The Buckwheat is an ideal starter spinning rod that is a substantial step forward from the slightly cheaper Greenhorn. This is an ultra-light rod, with the longest reach you’ll find at this price point.

items.name: Cunning Jafar
items.about: The Jafar is a legitimate antique that should only ever be bought from licensed, genuine merchants due to a popular black market trade that has formed around the rod. It was created as the height of luxury back in the day, but is no slouch by any means in the present. The Jafar was made to last, possessing a resolute sturdiness that feels right in your hand no matter the size or shape. The Jafar is such an iconic rod in the Perk’n’Kins brand, that many have reported insisting on being buried with it.

items.name: Devil’s Advocate
items.about: The Advocate is tailor made for empathic anglers who prefer to feel while they fish, connecting with the catch on a fundamental level. It’s for the sensitive angler who explores the world within themselves before they take a step outside.

items.name: Eisvogel
items.about: The Eisvogel is the lone spinning rod in the Rushy lineup, a formidable implement that came in the form of a flash of inspiration while angling at sea, and that spark was effortlessly converted to an exceptional freshwater rod in mere moments. The Eisvogel is everything you’ve come to expect from Rushy; heavy behemoths that catch heavy behemoths, but this is the smallest and quickest of the bunch.

items.name: Fairest of Them All
items.about: Mirror Carp, Mirror Carp on my wall, who is the fairest of them all? The fish holds no answers, and your wealth knows no limits. Truly then, you must be the most beautiful! You’re definitely the richest, and if there’s any difference you sure can’t spend it, so it definitely doesn’t matter.

items.name: Gold Monkey

This particular rod was much loved by the miners of Hartlepool, who found the extra casting exertion required kept them warm in even the harshest northern winters; the rod slotting seamlessly into their traditional winter wear, a pair of shorts and a blue-and-white striped polyester vest.

items.name: Goldhorn
items.about: The Goldhorn is modelled after the rod given to the very first Junior at the inception of the brand, and is the kind of implement that could inspire anyone to take up fishing if they have a spark for the hobby. It doesn’t get much easier to use than this, yet the rod still lies within the lexicon of competitive fishing due to it being the first foray into the sport for journeymen and experts alike.

items.about: The Harpunen boasts in associated advertising material that it could easily land any number of blue whales, and while nobody in their right mind would take that claim seriously, it remains relatively untested and wholly obnoxious. This is the rod for a modern angler with more money than sense, and more sense than actual friends.

items.name: Maiden
items.about: The very first prototype of the Maiden was originally made to celebrate the birth of Frank Rosenbaum’s fourth child, Smallmouth Rosenbaum, with the expectation that Smallmouth would eventually grow into the adult-sized rod. The construction of the rod was as indubitably sound as always, and after all comers were utterly ousted at the pre-schooler angling gauntlet, many curious parents inquired about where they could get themselves a version, thus giving birth to the Maiden.

items.name: Scran Snagger
items.about: The Scran Snagger in it’s original incarnation was a conceptualised as the kind of rod that would proudly place you on the pinnacle of a beach-side BBQ, however the cost-efficient nature of the rod soon angled it towards being a monumental step forward for journeyman sports fishing.

items.name: Vizier
items.about: The Vizier is a classic re-imagined for modern minds, based off the blueprint of the classic Jafar but with modern materials and sensibilities. It emphasizes the sturdiness and reliability of its predecessor without the sluggishness of surplus weight.

items.name: Vredesbringaren
items.about: This rod requires the Fiskespro Gear Pack DLC.

items.name: X85 Marksman
items.about: The X85 Marksman is a solid all-rounder that offers a level of precision and excellence in anything it tackles. As the name suggests, the marksman is made from rifle parts, although isn’t quite as specialised as a sniper in the way that it functions, performing more like an angling assault rifle.

items.name: X86 Marksman
items.about: The X86 Marksman is like the younger sibling of the X85: Different in some ways, but similar enough to feel instantly familiar. Utilizing the same design, the X86 is made from lighter materials compared to its sibling but still offers the same performance.

items.name: Y934 Romulus
items.about: The Romulus is a lightweight spinning rod that provides perfect military-grade precision without weighing down free movement. It is a sleek schooner of an implement, lapping the heavier battleships and displacing the tiny dinghies other brands offer up for the same price.

items.name: Canny Workieticket
items.about: The Workieticket hails from the frigid tundra of North-East England, whereupon the schematic was described by way of interpreter through veil of gravy to Larry Wright, head engineer and tuck shop gaffer of the Wright enterprise. Larry was eager to learn the customs of these strange and wondrous people, especially of the way they lived and fished, and after emerging a number of weeks later south of the border began work on the rod with nothing more than a hazy memory and something scrawled on his hand. Within months a prototype of Workieticket was given form, a peerless all-rounder in the realm of baitcasting.

items.name: Chief Consul
items.about: The Consul is a baitcasting rod for the life of the party, a sociable, outgoing and gregarious angler who is an encouragement to those that fish beside them. It is also, quite simply, one of the very best money can buy, offering colossal weight and power at the expense of length and range.

items.name: D30 Remus
items.about: The D30 Remus is a baitcasting battleship, offering weight and heft that it’s brother simply can’t. Even though the Romulus can run rings around the Remus, the latter’s pure power blows all competition out of the water.

items.name: Daring Virtuoso

It’s said that in the Black Forest, lifting a Graureiher over your head is considered a rite of passage, and as such from an early age many other brands of rods are imported so the locals can work their way up.

items.about: The Kormoran is one of the Rushy baitcasting twins, offering a relative depth of deftness and manoeuvrability while still being heavier and slower than practically anything else. It’s said that in order to have your name carved into the hallowed Rushy tree of fame deep inside the Black Forest, one must be able to catch a local fish with every rod in the Rushy lineup. The Kormoran is always the first in the challenge, and for many, the last.

items.name: Shahryar
items.about: The Shahryar still follows the recipe of making modern musterings that feel and perform just like the classics you remember, but this time aim accurately to be an all-round rod for a seasoned fishing aficionado.

A crest proudly emblazoned with Northumberland tartan, a county itself made through montage in much the same way. This poor-man’s racehorse has eaten well and grown long, supplanting many austere diamonds to be a genuine Geordie gem.

intro: Fishing reels are an essential component of any angler’s setup, playing a pivotal role in casting, retrieving, and battling fish. Choosing the right reel is crucial for ensuring a successful and enjoyable fishing experience. Reels come in various designs, each tailored for specific techniques and skill levels, making it important to understand their differences and advantages. From beginner-friendly spinning reels to the precision-driven baitcasting reels, there’s a reel to match every angler’s needs.

In Call of the Wild: The Angler game, reels are split into two main categories, Spinning Reels and Baitcasting Reels, with a third that never made it into the game. Below is a list of all available reels in the game.

The fly fishing reel cannot be used. It has no name or price of its own, and no rod will take it: every rod is a spinning, match, baitcasting or bottom rod, and none of them accepts a fly reel. It is listed here because fly fishing was built a long way before it was dropped, down to three reel models, interface icons and a full first-person casting animation set, which makes it a cut feature rather than an oversight.

items.name: Belta
items.about: The Belta is the only spinning reel on Wright’s menu and it sure is something, offering a considerable line capacity and gear ratio combo for a high range and speedy retrieval. Every single spinning setup Wright has marketed has boasted a Belta, and there’s very little evidence of that changing any time soon.

items.name: Belta 2.0
items.about: After years of sticking to its single spinning reel, Wright has released their re-imagining of the classic Belta. Boasting similar line capacity and gear ratio combo, the Belta 2.0 has been created for a higher weight segment of fishing – combining the best of both worlds.

items.name: Blue Prince
items.about: This reel was part of the Special Event.

items.name: Brugden
items.about: The Brugden is Fiskespr?’s top spinning reel and easily one of the best available today, pairing an exemplary gear ratio for lightning fast line retrieval with rock-solid fundamentals.

items.name: Camarón
items.about: This is the Camarón reel in Call of the Wild: The Angler.

items.name: Cassio
items.about: The Othello is the finest spinning reel in the Perk’n’Kins catalog, taking the recipe of the Iago and bringing it up to speed. In many ways, the Othello-Shahryar combo are the modern re-imagining of the classic Iago-Jafar combo, transforming that classic combo into something that will continue to stand the test of time.

items.name: Champion
items.about: The Champion is a reel that fits those that prize pure catching potential and competitive performance above all else. Surprisingly, this was created in partnership with the Wright brand, although they aren’t formally credited, bridging the gap between England and Tokyo in a powerful fashion.

items.name: Cria
items.about: The Cria is another entry level offering from Junior, unifying the brand as the best possible first fishing experience for all-comers. In a charity outreach program with Brooklyn zoo, the Cria was chosen as the reel given to chimps in a fishing exhibition, although results were mixed.

items.name: Epilogue
items.about: The Prologue is the start of something special. Nothing to write home about, but you won’t forget it when you’re famous.

items.name: Festivus for the Rest of Us

items.name: Hund

items.name: Iago
items.about: The Iago was originally designed to sit alongside the Jafar as a powerful team, maximizing each other’s strengths and compensating for their weaknesses. Over time, they have been separated within the zeitgeist of modern fishing, a movement largely propelled by the scarcity of the respective tackle and difficulty in procuring both parts. Running them both together still remains a classic combination, and that level of synchronization and synergy never goes out of style.

items.name: Kitay
items.about: A stunningly constructed tribute to the Ainu people of the Kamuibetsu region. Named after the Ainu word for “Peak”, Kitay is as effective a tool as it is a piece of art. Cherish it.

items.name: Rüttelflug
items.about: The Rüttelflug is considered the king of spinning reels, preceded by its own fantastical mythology that shrouds its every operation in mystery. It was considered lost for decades before a sequestered cache resurfaced within the Black Forest, bubbling forth into select high level competition across the globe.

items.name: Scope
items.about: The Scope is a mid tier spinning reel that introduced the world to the hallmark precision that cut Räckvidd’s teeth. It boasts a relatively fast line retrieval speed for the price, which leads to a quick, decisive and responsive angling experience.

items.about: The Tauch was created as a replacement after the Rüttelflug was thought to have been completely lost to time. It pales in comparison to its predecessor, but it sure takes the biscuit compared to the rest of the market.

items.name: Tyro
items.about: The Tyro is a fantastic way to ease yourself into a new fishing hobby, feeling quick and responsive beyond its meagre price. Many famous anglers have started out using a Greenhorn-Tyro combo, earning it the title of ‘The Perfect Start’.

items.name: Blåkäxa
items.about: The Blåkäxa is a pioneering baitcasting reel, combining a dynamic and daring design with brilliant build quality and an abrasive attitude. Despite any prior predilections you may possess, this is an all-round exceptional reel that is well worth the considerable price tag.

items.name: Colt
items.about: The Colt is considered to be a fantastic transitional reel, offering an unbelievable maximum drag that even considerably more expensive reels will struggle to match. For the Junior brand however, it’s their top offering and while they hope it’s all you’ll ever need, they understand that everyone needs to go somewhere, even if that’s into the arms of another home.

items.name: Dead Mint
items.about: The Mint was moniker-less for many years, however the consensus christened it with its current title via way of deafening proclamations during use. This is the best baitcasting reel Wright peddle to punters, a sublime mid tier performer that still remains relatively affordable.

items.name: Director
items.about: The Director is an exemplary baitcasting reel that shares the accolade of being the finest money can buy with its brother, the Mediator. This reel suits those who focus more on speed and deftness than pure power.

items.name: Keen Shoat
items.about: The Shoat is a meaningful step up for any beginner, without an extortionate price hike that could scare them off the sport forever. What this model has over the Cria and Tyro is a substantial increase in max drag, bolstering the power that the rod can spit out during a catch.

items.name: Mediator
items.about: The Mediator is a fantastic baitcasting reel that sits alongside the Director as the best money can buy. This reel fits those that care a lot more about power and reliability rather than catching fish quickly.

items.name: Montano
items.about: The Montano is marketed as the last baitcasting reel you’ll ever need, and while it isn’t anything incredible in the power department, its signature speed and capacity are certainly enough to give that claim some consideration. This is based on a vintage reel design that was the hallmark of the 20th century auction scene, except reforged with brand new technology and keen artistry to result in a great angling experience.

items.name: Muckle
items.about: The Muckle is a large, sturdy and structurally sound baitcasting reel prized for its considerable line capacity to cost ratio, enabling some serious whoppers to be caught without breaking the bank. It was originally created for use in the Tyne river, where a day’s fishing can rapidly segue between a fish big enough to feed a family for a week or a conspicuous lump that is checked for change and reported to the authorities.

intro: The line is the one piece of tackle that touches every part of the fight, and its test weight is the single most consequential number in your setup. It caps what you can land, and it is part of how a catch is scored: a fish is worth 1,300 points per kilogram and the line costs 300 points per kilogram of its rating, so the same fish scores higher on lighter line.

That trade is the whole game. Land a fish heavier than the line is rated for and the charge comes back multiplied, which is where the largest scores come from; snap off and you get nothing. Fishing a rating just under what you expect to hook is the deliberate risk the scoring rewards.

The three types behave differently under load. Monofilament stretches, which forgives a heavy hand on the drag and a sudden lunge at the net. Fluorocarbon is the hardest to see underwater and sinks, so it suits clear water and wary fish. Braid has no stretch at all, so every knock reaches the rod tip and it is by far the strongest for its diameter, but it is highly visible and unforgiving of a tight drag.

Thickness matters as much as rating. A thinner line of the same strength casts further, sinks faster and is less visible, which is why braid at a given test weight fishes very differently from mono at the same number.

intro: The hook is the only part of your setup that actually holds the fish, and the one most often got wrong. Sizes run from 10 at the smallest up to 4/0 at the largest, counting down to 1 and then up through the /0 sizes, so a 1/0 is one step larger than a 1 rather than ten times smaller.

Two things constrain the choice. Every rod states a hook range it accepts, and every bait or lure states the size it is tied to. The hook has to satisfy both, which is why a heavy rod paired with a small bait often will not fish at all.

Bigger is not better. An oversized hook is visible to a wary fish and sits badly in a small mouth, so a fish will take at it and miss. Match the hook to the bait first and the rod second, and only go up a size when you are losing fish to pulled hooks rather than to refusals.

The shop stocks 10 down to 4/0. The six larger sizes carry no price in any currency and no shop stocks them, and every lure that asks for one is likewise unbuyable, so they are marked here rather than hidden.

intro: The reel speed is the 1x to 6x retrieve setting you change while reeling in. Every lure works at 1x to 6x on every retrieve it supports (the wiki says 1 to 5, but the game goes up to 6x). The wiki does not say which speed is best, and lists no speed for soft plastics on a jig head, so the speeds below are Steam player tips (unverified).

items.name: Shad
items.about: A plastic shad is a plastic fishing lure, generally made to simulate a small fish. Plastic shads can carry a variety of shapes, colors and sizes, and are made from a variety of synthetic polymers. The ‘shad’ are models that have a round tail, a peak that opposes displacement, that locks, and therefore causes turbulence. This part can be more or less perpendicular to the direction in which the lure is collected.

items.name: Worm
items.about: A plastic worm is a plastic fishing lure made to imitate an earthworm. Plastic worms can carry a variety of shapes, colors and sizes, and are made from many different synthetic polymers, and can be scented to simulate live bait. Plastic worms can be rigged on the line many different ways. Commonly they are used with a small fish hook and a split shot weight to keep the lure deeper in the water. A common fishing strategy is to configure them as a Texas rig, and bounce them off the bottom. The key is to jig near cover such as weeds and trees; this technique is commonly referred to as flipping and pitching.
